external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes the nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: The service loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where uploaded compliance documents stay.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The source says both that the nightly extract is encrypted end to end and that the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Suppliers sign in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and staff contact details to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and staff contact details

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: retrieve documents
data_flows.description: The portal retrieves uploaded documents from the vendor platform for review.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says the nightly extract is encrypted end to end, but the landing bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file
data_flows.notes: The source says the nightly extract is encrypted end to end, but the landing bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: supplier environment
trust_boundaries.description: The supplier-controlled side from which suppliers access the portal.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal presents a web interface because the text calls it a portal.
assumptions.basis: The source names the component 'Supplier document portal' and describes suppliers using it to upload paperwork and sign in.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier-controlled side is a separate tenant trust zone from the vendor and organisation-controlled environments.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers are described as actors accessing the vendor-hosted portal, but no more specific supplier location is stated.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's data is confidential because it contains compliance documents and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source says the platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's data is confidential because it receives supplier data extracts containing supplier records and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the bucket as receiving a supplier data extract, and the described supplier data includes contact details for staff.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's data is confidential because it contains supplier records originating from the supplier extract.
assumptions.basis: The source says the supplier master service writes supplier extract records into the supplier database.
